# Activate the Vault OAuth resource server

Vault gates OAuth resource server functionality behind an activation flag.
Vault returns errors for profile configuration and JWT authentication requests
until you activate the `oauth-resource-server` feature.

<Tabs>

<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

```shell-session
$ vault write -f sys/activation-flags/oauth-resource-server/activate

Key            Value
---            -----
activated      [oauth-resource-server]
unactivated    [secrets-import secrets-sync]
```

</Tab>

<Tab heading="API" group="api">

```shell-session
$ curl                                        \
    --request PUT                             \
    --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}"  \
    ${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/sys/activation-flags/oauth-resource-server/activate
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>

Once enabled, Vault acts as an OAuth 2.0 resource server with distinct OAuth
server profiles. Each profile tells Vault which issuer to trust, how to verify
token signatures, and which claims to enforce.
